title: Red spider mite on tomato - Kenya

Header: Red spider mite on tomato - Kenya

Prevention: Avoid planting new crop next to an infested field.
Avoid continuous cropping of tomato & Solanaceae plants (potato, eggplant, nightshades).
Intercrop tomato with repellent crops e.g. garlic, basil or onion.
Clean & disinfect stakes & twines with chlorine- based products.
Remove residues of previous susceptible plants and destroy them.
Minimize application of broadspectrum pesticides to conserve natural enemies (particularly predatory mites).
Avoid dusty conditions and water stress (irrigate crops regularly & apply mulch to reduce water evaporation).
Avoid high levels of nitrogen which will encourage spider mite reproduction.

Monitoring: Check for spots & fine webbing of brown or silvery colour on leaves & white speckling on fruits.
Check the lower leaves (underside) for reddish small mites (hand magnifying lens strongly recommended).
Consider action when on average about 10 spider mites per leaf are seen.
Restrictions: Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
When using a pesticide, always wear personal protective equipment and follow the instructions on the product label.
Toxic to aquatic life and bees, should not be used near waterways or during flowering.
